questions.question: Define habitat and adaptation, name the three kinds of adaptation, and give one South African example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A habitat is the place where an organism lives. An adaptation is an inherited feature that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its habitat. Structural: a body part or shape, such as the gemsbok's pale coat or the quiver tree's water-storing branches. Physiological (functional): how the body works, such as the gemsbok producing concentrated urine or letting its body temperature rise instead of sweating. Behavioural: something the organism does, such as the gemsbok feeding at night or geckos sheltering in burrows by day.

questions.question: Describe four adaptations that help plants survive in the Karoo or Kalahari.
questions.expected_answer: Storing water in thick, fleshy leaves, stems or roots (succulents such as the quiver tree and vygies); a waxy surface that reduces water loss; small leaves or spines that reduce the surface for evaporation and protect stored water from animals; opening leaf pores only at night when it is cooler; deep roots to reach groundwater (camel thorn) or shallow wide roots to catch brief rain; surviving the dry season as seeds and flowering after rain.

questions.question: Explain why a giraffe's long neck is an inherited adaptation rather than the result of stretching, and explain the difference between camouflage and warning colouration.
questions.expected_answer: Changes during a lifetime, such as stretching, are not passed on in genetic instructions. Giraffes vary at birth; those born with slightly longer necks reached more food in hard times, survived and had more offspring, which inherited the longer necks, and over many generations the population came to have long necks. Camouflage helps an animal blend into its surroundings so predators or prey do not see it (chameleon, stick insect). Warning colouration is bright, bold colour that advertises that an animal is poisonous or bad-tasting, so predators learn to avoid it (foam grasshopper).
